title: SEVENTEEN's V8 Sub-Unit Drops Debut EP with Pharrell Williams
summary: The 8 and Vernon are diving into the theme of "wasted youth" on the mini-album due out on June 29. SEVENTEEN members The 8 and VERNON are gearing up to launch the first mini-album from their new side unit, V8. The self-titled mini-album, due out on June 29, finds the K-pop duo teaming up with a long list of big-name producers, including former collaborator Pharrell Williams. According to a release announcing the project, it is a deep dive into the theme of "wasted youth," with the songs focused on "raw moments of wandering and confusion experienced through time, along with the resilience and growth found within those struggles. Rather than defining the youth spent as mere lost time, the album sublimates the unstable and fragile nature of youth into an explosive sense of freedom, channeling that energy into a driving force to continuously forge ahead." In addition to Pharrell - who produced the song "Bad Influence" from the group's fifth studio album, 2025's Happy Burstday - the mini-album will feature the pair working with longtime collaborator BUMZU, as well as a number of other producers, whose names were revealed in a clever video clip featuring the list burning in reverse to reveal the roster. Among the names on the paper are German electro house producer/DJ Mechatok, 100 Gecs' Dylan Brady, Korean Music Awards winner KIRARA, as well as a number of other pop, electronic and hip-hop producers, including: Alice Longyu Gao, BADTREE, HAKASEEE, Han Jung In, Jake Torrey, kimj, Lodge Boy, Lucian, MILLENNIUM, Numbernine, Ramzoid, Rhode, Robb Roy, Rudolph, Sophie Cates, Stella Smyth, UHD, and Will Not Fear. The duo teased their upcoming debut with a grainy 30-second video that included them lounging in an apartment, throwing food at each other and dancing through a shower of fireworks in front of a billboard featuring their group name, soundtracked by a snippet of their hyperpop sound. It's a bold, exciting new direction for the two artists.
why_it_matters: V8's exploration of wasted youth speaks directly to teenagers' feelings of uncertainty, and the global collaboration shows how music can cross borders to create something fresh and relatable.

background_read: SEVENTEEN is a 13-member K-pop boy band that debuted in 2015 and is known for writing and producing its own music, often splitting into sub-units for different genres.

Pharrell Williams is a Grammy-winning American musician, singer, and producer famous for hits like 'Happy' and for his work with The Neptunes, and he previously collaborated with SEVENTEEN on their 2025 album 'Happy Burstday.'
Hyperpop is a genre that emerged in the 2010s, defined by pitched-up vocals, digital distortion, and frantic beats; artists like 100 gecs helped popularize it.
BUMZU is a South Korean producer and songwriter who has worked with SEVENTEEN since their early days, often acting as a key musical partner in the group's creative direction.

perspectives.description: Fans are excited that The 8 and Vernon can showcase new artistic sides, and the involvement of Pharrell Williams and hyperpop producers boosts global attention for K-pop.
Some worry that sub-units can be a marketing tactic to keep the group's brand alive, and the hyperpop sound might alienate fans who prefer traditional K-pop.
Hyperpop remains a niche but influential genre; blending it with K-pop illustrates how Internet-era music quickly merges styles from different cultures.
If V8 succeeds, it could pave the way for more experimental K-pop sub-units and encourage collaboration between Western avant-garde producers and Korean artists.
